text:
reema: Quick brain dump: we need a lightweight "regional budget shim" in the policy stack to avoid noisy bursts triggering cross-region hedges. Idea: a tiny runtime signal (0..1) computed per tenant-region, plus a version tag. Policy reads it and can bias routing weights. Need thoughts on protocol and defaults.

jon: I like a simple float. Two questions: where is it computed and how often updated? Also how do we guarantee it's not spoofable?

mica: Compute in a small scorer service; each host has a local sidecar that caches scores. Sidecar talks to central state or keeps local sliding windows. Update every 1s or 2s. Sidecar signs header so runtime trusts it.

omar: Signing is key. Runtime must reject unsigned scores. Also prefer permissive default (score=1) if scorer unreachable, but emit an alert so ops can triage.

reema: Agreed. Proposed fields attached to request metadata: X-Redwood-Budget: "v1;tenant=acme;region=us-west;score=0.42;ts=...;sig=...". Policy exposes builtin fn `region_budget_score()` to read parsed header.

jon: Implementation tradeoffs: in-process lib vs sidecar. Lib = fastest, but rollout complexity + memory. Sidecar => easy rollback and uniform behaviour across runtimes. Leaning sidecar.

mica: Sidecar protocol: unix-socket for same-host, HTTP fallback for containers. Minimal JSON: {tenant, region, score, window_seconds, version}. Keep the payload tiny.

omar: TTL behaviour: score decays over time. Use sliding-exponential with half-life configurable per-tenant. Also store last-updated ts. If header older than TTL, runtime treats as stale and sets score=1 (permissive) but tags metric.

reema: DSL ergonomics: one runtime hook `region_budget_score()` which pulls from request meta or calls scorer when missing. Compiler must treat it as runtime-only. Add a macro `allow_if_cost_under_budget(cost)` for product folks.

jon: Tests: ensure compiler doesn't constant-fold the hook. Add a perf test where sidecar is saturated to ensure p99 impact < 5ms. Also unit test header parsing, signature verification, and stale handling.

mica: Migration plan: 1) deploy scorer & sidecar in staging; 2) opt-in tenants in shadow mode (decisions logged but not enforced) for 10 days; 3) small canary enforcement; 4) gradual rollout + dashboards. Add feature flag REDWOOD_REGIONAL_BUDGETS for emergency kill.

omar: Observability: histogram of scores, per-tenant flip-rate (how often policy changed route because of score), and fraction of requests with stale/missing score. Pager on >2% missing for >5m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: staged rollout triggered: feature/regional-budget-shim -> arch-staging (4 hosts) :rocket:

reema: Security note: sidecar must authenticate to central scorer via mTLS and rotate keys. Also audit log when operator manually refills a tenant's buffer.

jon: Edge-case: cross-region requests where two scores exist. Policy should see both (e.g., inbound header list) or we define precedence: prefer local region's score, then fallback to remote. Will document.

mica: I'll draft RFC with protocol, example headers, signer model, and DSL snippets. Omar, can you own runbook + metrics? Jon can add compiler guards. Reema will prototype sidecar.

reema: Great, will open PR with prototype and shadow-mode telemetry. Thanks all.
